items.note: Put 懂 after a perception verb to show that understanding is achieved through listening or another compatible action. For inability, place 不 between the perception verb and 懂. Learners often put the negation before the verb or insert 了 inside the verb-complement pair.

For a compatible monosyllabic verb, repeat the verb with 一 between the two copies to suggest a brief action or soften a suggestion. This pattern is not for every verb. Learners often move 一 out of the middle or omit one copy of the verb.

items.en: Take a look at this.
items.wrongPy: kàn yí kàn yí zhè ge
items.why: 一 belongs between the repeated verbs; placing another 一 before the demonstrative makes the phrase ungrammatical.

items.note: Place 回来 or 回去 after the action phrase to show a return toward or away from the speaker. The choice of 来 or 去 depends on viewpoint. Learners often put 回 before the action or separate it from 来 or 去.

Use 没有 between the item being compared and the reference, then put the adjective after the reference. This says the first item is not as adjective as the second. Learners often place the adjective before the reference; keep it after both items.

items.en: This bag is not as big as that bag.
items.wrongPy: zhè ge bāo méi yǒu dà nà ge bāo
items.why: The adjective follows the reference item; say 这个包没有那个包大。

items.note: Place 往 before a direction or destination, then add the motion phrase. Use it to say where movement is headed. Learners often put the direction before 往; keep 往 directly before the direction or place.

items.en: This road is a little longer.
items.wrongPy: zhè tiáo lù yì diǎnr cháng
items.why: 一点儿 follows 长 in this pattern, so say 这条路长一点儿。

items.note: Place 自己 after the verb when it is the reflexive object, referring back to the subject. Learners should not repeat 自己: one instance is enough to express that the wife or husband acts on themself.

Use 有 followed by a number and measurement to state an age, size, length, or amount. Learners may reorder the measurement and description or add 个 before a unit that does not take it; keep the measure in its standard form.

items.en: This road is ten li long.
items.wrongPy: zhè tiáo lù yǒu shí gè lǐ cháng
items.why: 里 does not take 个 in this measurement; say 这条路有十里长。

items.en: That road is ten li long.
items.wrongPy: nà tiáo lù yǒu shí gè lǐ cháng
items.why: 里 does not take 个 in this measurement; say 那条路有十里长。

items.note: Use 跟 between two noun phrases to link people or things that share a predicate. It does not join two full clauses. Learners often put 跟 next to the predicate instead of directly between the two noun phrases.

Use 是 before a noun phrase that characterizes the subject, such as a color or a type of person. This is not ordinary class membership; learners often move 是 after the description or put 的 inside the noun phrase.
For a brief, bounded action, repeat a one-syllable verb with 了 between the two copies. Learners often put 了 after the repeated verb or between the object and verb.
Put 比 between the compared item and the reference, then state the adjective, usually without neutral 很. Learners often place the adjective before the reference or add 很 mechanically.
Use 有时 or 有时候 before the action to say it happens sometimes. 有时候 is a fuller variant; learners may mistakenly split it or put 时 after the verb.

items.en: I sometimes go out for a walk.
items.wrongPy: wǒ shí hou yǒu chū mén zǒu lù
items.why: Put 有时候 before the action phrase; the correct phrase is 我有时候出门走路。

items.note: Sentence-final 啊 adds warmth, emphasis, or an expressive spoken tone. Put it after the whole statement, as in these exclamations. Learners sometimes place 啊 inside the predicate; here it belongs at the end.
Use 再 before the next action to show that it follows the first one. It does not have to mean doing something again. Learners may put 再 between a verb and its object, where it breaks the verb phrase.

items.en: Class ends, then go home.
items.wrongPy: xià kè zài jiā huí
items.why: 家 must come after 回 in this phrase; the correct order is 下课，再回家。

items.en: I’ll look, then write the characters.
items.wrongPy: wǒ kàn le zài hàn zì xiě
items.why: 再 should precede the complete action 写汉字; the correct order is 我看了，再写汉字。

items.note: 虽然 introduces the conceded fact, and 但是 introduces the contrasting clause. Either connector can sometimes stand alone, but when both appear, learners should keep them with their respective clauses rather than combine or misorder them.
Use 但 or 但是 to introduce a contrasting clause; the first clause needs no concessive marker. Learners may wrongly add a concessive marker before it.
Put 左边 or 右边 after the reference noun to identify a location relative to it. Learners often put 左 or 右 before the reference noun instead of after it.
Use 因为 before the cause and 所以 before the result; either connector can be omitted when the relationship is clear. Learners often put 不 before the subject instead of directly before the verb.
Use 是...还是... to ask someone to choose between two clauses; initial 是 may be omitted. Learners often put a destination before 去, although the verb should precede it.
Use 还是 between alternatives in a direct choice question, often without a full sentence. Do not append 吗: 还是 already marks the choice question, so 吗 clashes with the intended question form.
Put a subject-predicate clause before 的 to describe a following noun, as in 你打的鱼. The common mistake is placing 的 after the noun; it must separate the complete modifying clause from that noun.
Repeat a monosyllabic adjective and add 的 before the noun for a vivid description, as in 小小的鸟. Do not put predicate words between 的 and the noun it modifies.

items.en: The tiny bird is very pretty.
items.wrongPy: xiǎo xiǎo de hěn piào liang niǎo
items.why: 很漂亮 splits 的 from the noun; 小小的 must directly modify 鸟.

items.note: 好 + adjective expresses a high degree, often as an immediate reaction: 好热！ A common mistake is putting 好 after the adjective instead of before it.

items.en: It’s so hot!
items.wrongPy: rè hǎo
items.why: 好 comes before 热 in this emphatic pattern, not after it.

items.en: I’m so tired; I’d better go to sleep.
items.wrongPy: lèi hǎo hái shi shuì jiào ba
items.why: 好 must come before 累; the phrase should begin 好累。

items.note: In a topic-comment sentence, the first phrase establishes what you are talking about, and the following subject-predicate clause says something about it. Use this when the comment is related to, but not simply identical with, the topic. Learners may wrongly force the topic to be the clause’s grammatical subject.

已经 marks something as true or completed by a relevant reference time; 了 commonly appears after the predicate to indicate a resulting change or current relevance. Use the final 了 when the context supports it, not mechanically in every 已经 sentence. Learners often place 了 before the predicate.

Put 完 immediately after a verb to show that the action has been completed; the object, if any, normally follows the verb-result unit. Use it for finished actions, while noting that negated completion does not necessarily mean the action never began. Learners often put 完 after the object.

Put 最 directly before an adjective to mark the highest degree in a comparison set understood from context. It can describe an adjective phrase such as 有意思 or 好. Learners often put 最 after the adjective; it must come before it.
Use 还是 before the action you recommend and 吧 after it to make a suggestion after considering alternatives. Learners often put 吧 inside the verb phrase instead of at the end.

items.en: We’d better walk.
items.wrongPy: hái shi ba zǒu lù
items.why: 吧 belongs after 走路, not after 还是; say 还是走路吧。

items.en: Let's go in after all.
items.wrongPy: wǒ men hái shi ba jìn qù
items.why: 吧 belongs at the end of the suggestion; say 我们还是进去吧。

items.note: 好多 comes before a noun to mean an informal, unspecified large quantity. It can also occur in the separate expression 好多了 meaning “much better”; learners often misread that expression as 好多 followed by a noun.

items.en: There are lots of hotels in foreign countries.
items.wrongPy: wài guó hǎo duō yǒu jiǔ diàn
items.why: 好多酒店 must stay together after 有; the correct order is 外国有好多酒店。

items.en: Lots of children are outside.
items.wrongPy: hǎo duō xiǎo háir wài miàn zài
items.why: 在 must precede the location phrase; the correct order is 好多小孩儿在外面。

items.note: 快 + verb phrase + 了 says an event is imminent, not that someone performs it quickly. Place 了 after the whole verb phrase. Learners often put 了 directly after 快 instead of after the event.

items.en: Class will be over soon.
items.wrongPy: kuài le xià kè
items.why: 了 belongs after 下课, not after 快; the correct order is 快下课了。

items.en: They are about to go abroad.
items.wrongPy: tā men kuài le chū guó
items.why: 了 follows the event 出国; the correct order is 她们快出国了。

items.note: Place a path marker after a motion verb, then 来 or 去 to show movement toward or away from the speaker. Learners often reverse the order or confuse 来 and 去.

items.en: The bird flies up.
items.wrongPy: niǎo fēi qù shàng
items.why: Put 上 before 去; the correct phrase is 鸟飞上去.

items.en: Go up now.
items.wrongPy: nǐ kuài shàng qù lái ba
items.why: Use only one orientation marker here; the correct phrase is 你快上去吧。

items.en: Let's go in after all.
items.wrongPy: wǒ men hái shi lái jìn ba
items.why: Put 进 before the orientation marker; the correct phrase is 我们还是进去吧。

items.note: Put 这么 or 那么 before an adjective to express a degree established by context, like “this/that so.” Learners may place the degree word after the adjective; it belongs before the adjective, not after it.

items.en: The subway is so fast!
items.wrongPy: dì tiě kuài nà me
items.why: 那么 must come before 快, as in the correct phrase 地铁那么快！

items.note: For this existence pattern, put a place first, then a verb, then 着 before the thing that exists in that position or state. A quantity may come before the noun. Learners often put 着 after the noun; note that 有 can also express existence without 着.

items.en: There are lots of children sitting by the door.
items.wrongPy: mén kǒu zuò hǎo duō zhe xiǎo háir
items.why: 着 must follow 坐 and precede 好多小孩儿, as in the correct phrase 门口坐着好多小孩儿。

items.en: A lot of children are sitting at the bus stop.
items.wrongPy: chē zhàn zuò hǎo duō zhe xiǎo háir
items.why: 着 must follow 坐 and precede 好多小孩儿, as in the correct phrase 车站坐着好多小孩儿。

items.note: Put 面 after a direction word to name a side or location, such as the north side or the front. Established compounds may reduce its tone, but 面 still follows the direction; learners often reverse the two parts.

Use 比 to compare two items, then put the adjective and 多了 after the reference. 多了 marks a large difference rather than an exact count; learners often move it before the adjective or treat it as a precise number.
Use 每 plus a measure word and noun to refer to every member or occasion; 一 may precede the measure word, and 都 normally comes before the predicate. Learners often put 都 inside the noun phrase.

items.phrase: 小时候我每个星期都出去
items.zh: 小时候我每个星期都出去。
items.en: When I was a child, I went out every week.
items.wrong: 小时候每个我星期都出去。
items.wrongPy: xiǎo shí hou měi gè wǒ xīng qī dōu chū qù
items.why: 我 must precede 每个星期, so say 小时候我每个星期都出去。

items.note: Use a number directly before a conventional numbered unit, such as a floor label. This construction can omit 第 in established contexts; learners wrongly assume 第 is always required or put the unit before the number.

items.en: The hotel is on the third floor.
items.wrongPy: jiǔ diàn zài lóu sān
items.why: For this floor label, the number comes before the unit; swapping them does not name the intended floor.

items.en: I’ll wait for you on the third floor.
items.wrongPy: wǒ zài lóu sān děng nǐ
items.why: For this floor label, the number comes before the unit; swapping them does not name the intended floor.

items.note: Here 跟 introduces the person who accompanies or interacts with the subject, and the verb phrase follows that person. Use it for shared activities or interactions, not simply to join two subjects. Learners often put the person after the verb, copying English “with me” placement.

items.en: He walks with me.
items.wrongPy: tā gēn zǒu lù wǒ
items.why: The companion must follow 跟 and precede the activity; the correct phrase is “他跟我走路.”

items.en: I exercise with her.
items.wrongPy: wǒ gēn yùn dòng tā
items.why: The companion must follow 跟 and precede the activity; the correct phrase is “我跟她运动.”

items.en: I’ll go upstairs with him.
items.wrongPy: wǒ gēn shàng qù tā
items.why: The companion must follow 跟 and precede the activity; the correct phrase is “我跟他上去.”

items.en: I swam with Grandma when I was little.
items.wrongPy: xiǎo shí hou wǒ gēn yóu yǒng nǎi nai
items.why: The companion must follow 跟 and precede the activity; the correct phrase is “小时候我跟奶奶游泳.”

items.note: Use 从 before the route or place, followed by the motion phrase. It can describe a path or passage, not only where someone starts. Learners often put 从 after the motion phrase; keep it before the route.

items.en: Go out from the station.
items.wrongPy: cóng chū qù chē zhàn
items.why: The place must follow 从 and precede the motion phrase; say 从车站出去。

items.en: We’ll go in through the doorway.
items.wrongPy: wǒ men zǒu jìn qù cóng mén kǒu
items.why: 从门口 must come before the motion phrase; say 我们从门口走进去。

items.note: Use 要 or 快要 before a verb phrase and 了 at the end to say an event is imminent. The pattern highlights that something is about to happen, rather than merely describing a distant plan. Learners often put 了 in the wrong place or omit it, losing the imminent meaning.

items.en: He is going abroad soon.
items.wrongPy: tā yào le chū guó le
items.why: 了 cannot follow 要 here; put it after the verb phrase, as in 他要出国了。

items.en: He is about to come back.
items.wrongPy: tā kuài yào le huí lai
items.why: 了 must follow the verb phrase, so the correct order is 他快要回来了。

items.en: They are about to go traveling.
items.wrongPy: tā men kuài yào chū qù le lǚ yóu
items.why: 了 must follow the whole verb phrase, so say 他们快要出去旅游了。

items.note: Put 过 after a verb to say that someone has had an experience before, without narrating one specific completed event. Learners often place 过 before the verb or mistake it for a marker that can freely move around the sentence.

items.en: I have lived abroad.
items.wrongPy: wǒ guò zài wài guó zhù
items.why: 过 follows the verb 住, so the correct sentence is 我在外国住过。

items.note: Put a number and 次 after the verb to count how many times an action occurs. 次 counts action occurrences, not objects. Learners often attach it to the object or reverse the order of the number and 次.
Use 为什么 before the predicate to ask why something happens or is the case. A 为什么 question already asks for a reason, so learners should not add 吗 as a second question marker.

Use 从 + a starting time + a verb phrase to say when a continuing or repeated action began. It works for actions that continue or recur from that point onward. Learners may put part of the verb phrase before the starting-time marker or move 都 out of its usual position.

items.en: I have studied Chinese since I was little.
items.wrongPy: cóng xiǎo shí hou xué kāi shǐ zhōng wén
items.why: 开始 should come before the whole verb phrase 学中文, not split it apart.

items.note: Put 的 after a modifier to let it stand for an understood noun, as in “the red one” or “the young ones.” The phrase with 的 can fill a noun-like role in a sentence. Learners may omit 的 or place it inside a fixed location phrase such as 在上面.

Use a trigger clause followed by 就 and a result clause to show a consequence or the next event prompted by the first clause. The trigger may be a condition or an event. Learners may put 就 in the trigger clause or separate a verb from its result complement.

Use 那 at the start of a statement to connect it to what was just said, meaning “in that case” or “then.” It introduces a discourse consequence rather than modifying a noun. Learners may move 那 after the subject and mistake its role in the sentence.

items.en: Then I’ll get ready to travel.
items.wrongPy: wǒ nà zhǔn bèi lǚ yóu
items.why: 那 should introduce the consequent statement before 我, not follow the subject.

items.note: Put a verb phrase before 的 and the noun it describes. Use this pattern to identify a noun by an action, such as who gave a gift or what a class teaches. Learners often put 的 after the noun or omit it, breaking the modifier structure.

就要 + verb phrase + 了 presents an event as imminent; an explicit time expression can also appear before the pattern. Learners often put 了 inside the verb phrase, but it belongs at the end of the sentence.

items.en: The exam is about to begin.
items.wrongPy: jiù le yào kǎo shì
items.why: 了 cannot come between 就 and 要; it belongs after the verb phrase, as in 就要考试了.

items.note: An early time expression followed by 就 + verb phrase says the event happens earlier than expected, based on context. Learners often put 就 inside the verb or verb-object phrase; keep the whole verb phrase intact after 就.

items.en: Go to school as early as the morning.
items.wrongPy: zǎo shang shàng jiù xué
items.why: 上学 is the verb phrase and must stay together after 就; 上就学 breaks it incorrectly.

items.note: Use a rounded number, 多, a measure word, and then the noun to give an amount above that number but below the next round boundary. Learners often put the measure word after the noun or duplicate it.
With a compatible transfer verb, put 给 before the recipient and the thing after the recipient. Learners often put the thing first; that order is wrong here.

items.en: I sent her a packet of green tea.
items.wrongPy: wǒ sòng gěi yì bāo lǜ chá tā
items.why: 给 must be followed by the recipient, then the thing; the correct order is 我送给她一包绿茶.

items.en: I give her a packet of coffee.
items.wrongPy: wǒ sòng gěi yì bāo kā fēi tā
items.why: 给 must be followed by the recipient, then the thing; the correct order is 我送给她一包咖啡.

items.note: Use 得 after an action verb to describe how well or in what manner the action actually happens. It evaluates performance, not whether someone can do the action. Learners often confuse this with the potential complement or place 得 before the verb.

items.en: I have a great time with her.
items.wrongPy: wǒ gēn tā guò hěn de kuài lè
items.why: The complement marker must follow the verb directly; the correct order is verb, marker, then the degree phrase.

items.note: For literal downward motion, 下来 and 下去 follow a motion verb; 来 points toward the speaker, while 去 points away. Learners can reverse the parts or choose the wrong direction marker.

items.en: He went down from upstairs.
items.wrongPy: tā cóng lóu shàng zǒu qù xià
items.why: 下去 follows the motion verb in that order; the correct sentence is 他从楼上走下去.

items.en: He walked down from upstairs.
items.wrongPy: tā cóng lóu shàng zǒu lái xià le
items.why: 下来 must follow the motion verb in that order; the correct sentence is 他从楼上走下来了.

items.en: He walked down from upstairs.
items.wrongPy: tā cóng lóu shàng zǒu qù xià le
items.why: 下去 must follow the motion verb in that order; the correct sentence is 他从楼上走下去了.

items.note: 万 groups numbers by ten thousand, so put the number directly before 万, then add any remainder. Keep 零 when an internal place is skipped. Learners often put 万 after the money measure word or reverse the number and 万.

For an elapsed action duration, 了 usually follows the verb and the duration follows 了; an object may appear in different positions depending on its type. Learners often put 了 inside the duration phrase or scramble its words.

items.en: A few weeks passed.
items.wrongPy: guò jǐ le zhōu
items.why: 了 cannot split 几周; the correct phrase is 过了几周。

items.en: Worked for a few hours.
items.wrongPy: gōng zuò jǐ le xiǎo shí
items.why: 了 must follow 工作 and precede the duration; the correct phrase is 工作了几小时。

items.note: Use 了 for a completed event or 过 for experience, then place 次 after the verb aspect and any object. Learners often put 次 before 过.

items.en: I have taken the exam three times.
items.wrongPy: kǎo sān cì guò
items.why: 过 must follow the verb and precede the count; the correct phrase is 考过三次。

items.en: How many times has he taken the exam?
items.wrongPy: tā kǎo jǐ cì guò
items.why: 过 belongs before 几次, not after it; the correct question is 他考过几次？

items.note: 一……就…… links a trigger to an immediate result or a regular response. Put 一 before the trigger and 就 before the result clause; learners often place 就 before the subject instead.

items.en: As soon as I enter the classroom, class starts.
items.wrongPy: yí jiù jìn jiào shì shàng kè
items.why: 一 must precede the trigger action, not 就; the correct order is 一进教室，就上课。

items.en: As soon as the term starts, I go online.
items.wrongPy: yì kāi xué wǒ jiù wǎng shàng
items.why: 上网 is the verb phrase and cannot be reordered as 网上 here; the correct phrase is 一开学，我就上网。

items.en: As soon as the package arrives, I’ll open it.
items.wrongPy: bāo yì lái sòng wǒ jiù dǎ kāi
items.why: 送来 must stay in that order for “be delivered”; the correct phrase is 包一送来，我就打开。

items.en: As soon as I opened the package, I saw a notebook.
items.wrongPy: yì dǎ kāi bāo jiù běn zi kàn jiàn
items.why: 看见 must precede its object 本子; the correct phrase is 一打开包，就看见本子。

items.phrase: 一看见她就送她一包咖啡
items.zh: 一看见她，就送她一包咖啡。
items.en: As soon as I see her, I give her a packet of coffee.
items.wrong: 一看见她，就送一包她咖啡。
items.wrongPy: yí kàn jiàn tā jiù sòng yì bāo tā kā fēi
items.why: 她 must come before 一包咖啡 as the recipient; the correct phrase is 一看见她，就送她一包咖啡。

items.note: Put 给 before the person who receives or benefits from the action, then say the verb phrase. Use this with actions compatible with a recipient; learners often put the person after the verb or place 给 immediately before the verb.

items.en: Let me recommend a pharmacy to you.
items.wrongPy: wǒ gěi jiè shào nǐ yào diàn
items.why: 你 must follow 给 before the verb phrase; the correct order is 我给你介绍药店。

items.note: An affected thing can be the subject of an event predicate without 被, as in 包送到了. Use this when the context and verb support it; learners may wrongly put the event before its subject.

items.en: The fish has gone bad.
items.wrongPy: yú le huài
items.why: 了 follows the predicate here, not the subject; the correct phrase is 鱼坏了。

items.en: The package was delivered.
items.wrongPy: bāo dào le sòng
items.why: 送到 must stay together in that order; the correct phrase is 包送到了。

items.en: The fish may have spoiled.
items.wrongPy: yú huài kě néng le
items.why: 可能 must precede 坏了; the correct phrase is 鱼可能坏了。

items.en: The matter is taken care of.
items.wrongPy: shì qing le zuò hǎo
items.why: 了 follows the completed predicate 做好; the correct phrase is 事情做好了。

items.en: The notebook is ready.
items.wrongPy: běn zi hǎo zhǔn bèi le
items.why: 好 follows 准备 as its result complement; the correct phrase is 本子准备好了。

items.note: 是……的 highlights a circumstance such as when, where, how, or by whom a known event happened. Put 是 before the focused circumstance and 的 after the verb phrase; 是 is often optional.

items.en: The package was sent during New Year.
items.wrongPy: bāo shì guò nián shí sòng de lái
items.why: 的 must follow the full verb phrase 送来; the correct phrase is 包是过年时送来的。

items.note: Verb + 好 marks an action reaching a satisfactory or ready result, rather than merely stopping. Use it when the result is complete and suitable. Learners often put 好 before the verb or place 了 before 好.

items.en: The matter is taken care of.
items.wrongPy: shì qing zuò le hǎo
items.why: 好 must follow 做 and precede 了; the correct phrase is 事情做好了。

items.en: The notebook is ready.
items.wrongPy: běn zi zhǔn bèi le hǎo
items.why: 好 must follow 准备 and precede 了; the correct phrase is 本子准备好了。

items.en: The tickets are ready.
items.wrongPy: mén piào zhǔn bèi le hǎo
items.why: 好 must follow 准备 and precede 了; the correct phrase is 门票准备好了。

items.note: Verb + 错 marks an action that produces an incorrect result, as in answering or drawing something incorrectly. Use it when the action itself leads to an error. Learners often put 了 before 错 instead of after it.

items.en: He may have made a mistake on the test.
items.wrongPy: tā kě néng kǎo le cuò
items.why: 错 must follow 考 and precede 了; the correct phrase is 他可能考错了。

items.note: Put 别 immediately before the verb phrase to make a direct prohibition or preventive request. It can also precede a phrase beginning with 往 or 在. Learners sometimes place 别 after the person or place; keep it before the whole action phrase.

items.en: Don’t walk like that.
items.wrongPy: bié nǐ nà me zǒu
items.why: The subject 你 precedes 别; say 你别那么走。

items.en: Don't play soccer like that.
items.wrongPy: bié zú qiú nà me tī
items.why: 那么 must precede the verb and 足球 follows it; say 别那么踢足球。

items.note: 从 marks where motion starts, so put the starting place immediately after 从 and before the movement phrase. Learners often move the source after the motion; keep it in front.

items.en: Come up from downstairs.
items.wrongPy: nǐ xià miàn cóng shàng lái
items.why: 从 introduces the starting place before the motion phrase; the correct order is 你从下面上来.

items.en: He comes out of the shopping mall.
items.wrongPy: tā shāng chǎng cóng chū lái
items.why: 从 introduces the starting place before the motion phrase; the correct order is 他从商场出来.

items.en: Walk over from the front.
items.wrongPy: cóng zǒu guò qù qián miàn
items.why: 从 introduces the starting place before the motion phrase; the correct order is 从前面走过去.

items.en: He went down from upstairs.
items.wrongPy: tā cóng zǒu xià qù lóu shàng
items.why: 从 introduces the starting place before the motion phrase; the correct order is 他从楼上走下去.

items.en: Walk over there from the classroom.
items.wrongPy: cóng zǒu guò qù jiào shì ba
items.why: 从 introduces the starting place before the motion phrase; the correct order is 从教室走过去吧.

items.note: In an assertion, 几 + measure word + noun means “several” of something, as in 几个班. It can also ask “how many” in a question. Learners may use a measure word that does not fit the noun; choose one that matches the noun.
Put 来 or 去 after a motion verb to show movement toward or away from the contextual reference point. Learners often place the direction word before the verb or separate it from the verb phrase.

items.en: I’ll go upstairs with him.
items.wrongPy: wǒ tā gēn shàng qù
items.why: 他 must follow 跟, not come between the subject and verb; say 我跟他上去。

items.en: Come up from downstairs.
items.wrongPy: nǐ cóng shàng lái xià miàn
items.why: 下面 belongs after 从 and before 上来; say 你从下面上来。

items.en: Walk over from the front.
items.wrongPy: cóng zǒu guò qù qián miàn
items.why: 前面 must follow 从; say 从前面走过去。

items.en: He walks over from the front.
items.wrongPy: tā cóng zǒu guò lái qián miàn
items.why: 前面 must follow 从, before 走过来; say 他从前面走过来。

items.en: We play ball together.
items.wrongPy: yì qǐ wǒ men dǎ qiú
items.why: 一起 belongs after the subject and before the verb phrase; say 我们一起打球。

items.note: Use subject + 让 + person or affected thing + verb phrase to say that the subject lets, has, or causes someone to act or feel a certain way. Context determines whether 让 means “let” or “make.” Learners may put the affected person after the action; it goes after 让.

items.en: Exercise makes the body feel good.
items.wrongPy: yùn dòng ràng shēn tǐ shū fu hěn
items.why: 很 must come before the adjective 舒服; say 运动让身体很舒服。

items.note: Repeating a monosyllabic verb gives an action a brief, light, or tentative feel, often like “try” or “do a little.” Use the same verb twice together. Learners often move the object between the repeated verbs.

items.en: The teacher gives him a little test.
items.wrongPy: lǎo shī kǎo tā kǎo
items.why: The repeated verbs must stay together before the object; the correct phrase is 老师考考他。

items.en: Ask him, maybe.
items.wrongPy: nǐ wèn tā ba wèn
items.why: The repeated verbs must stay together before the object and 吧; the correct phrase is 你问问他吧。

items.en: The teacher will give you a little test.
items.wrongPy: lǎo shī kǎo nǐ men kǎo
items.why: The repeated verbs must stay together before the object; the correct phrase is 老师考考你们。

items.note: 常 and 经常 go before the verb phrase to say that an action happens often. Learners may put the frequency word after the action, but it belongs before the verb phrase in these examples.

items.en: He often swims.
items.wrongPy: tā yóu yǒng cháng
items.why: 常 must come before the verb phrase here; the correct sentence is 他常游泳.

items.en: We often play soccer.
items.wrongPy: wǒ men tī zú qiú cháng
items.why: 常 must come before the verb phrase here; the correct sentence is 我们常踢足球.

items.note: Use subject + 还没 + verb phrase to say an expected event has not happened yet; final 呢 is optional and adds a conversational tone. Learners may put 呢 inside the verb phrase, but it belongs at the end of the sentence.

items.en: He hasn't played soccer yet.
items.wrongPy: tā hái méi ne tī zú qiú
items.why: 呢 belongs at the end, after the verb phrase; say 他还没踢足球呢。

items.note: Put 这么、那么、这样, or 那样 before a verb phrase to describe how an action is done. In a negative command, 别 comes before the manner phrase and verb. Learners often put the manner word after the verb instead.

items.en: Don’t walk like that.
items.wrongPy: nǐ bié zǒu nà me
items.why: 那么 must come before 走, as in the correct phrase 你别那么走。

items.en: You play soccer this way.
items.wrongPy: nǐ tī zú qiú zhè me
items.why: 这么 must come before 踢足球, as in the correct phrase 你这么踢足球。

items.en: Don't play soccer like that.
items.wrongPy: bié tī zú qiú nà me
items.why: 那么 must come before 踢足球, as in the correct command 别那么踢足球。

items.note: Repeating a disyllabic verb in an ABAB pattern makes the action tentative or light, as in suggesting a little exercise or preparation. Use this only with verbs that allow reduplication. Learners often put 吧 inside the repeated verb.

items.en: Let’s exercise a little.
items.wrongPy: wǒ men yùn dòng ba yùn dòng
items.why: 吧 cannot split the repeated verb; the correct phrase is 我们运动运动吧。

items.en: Let’s get ready.
items.wrongPy: wǒ men zhǔn bèi ba zhǔn bèi
items.why: 吧 cannot split the repeated verb; the correct phrase is 我们准备准备吧。

items.note: For a compatible two-syllable adjective, repeat each syllable to form an AABB description, often before 地 when it modifies an action. Use it for vivid, lively descriptions. Learners often use 的 instead of 地 before the verb.

Put 多 immediately before the adjective in an exclamation ending in 啊. This expresses a high degree, as in “so fun,” rather than asking how much. Learners often move 多 after the adjective, where it no longer forms this exclamatory pattern.

items.en: Soccer is so much fun!
items.wrongPy: zú qiú hǎo wánr duō a
items.why: 多 must come before the adjective in this exclamation; “足球多好玩儿啊” is correct.

items.en: Exercise is so interesting!
items.wrongPy: yùn dòng yǒu yì si duō a
items.why: 多 must come before the adjective in this exclamation; “运动多有意思啊” is correct.

items.note: Place 多 after the measure word and before the noun to mean slightly more than the stated amount; it works with divisible units such as hours or months. Learners often put 多 before the measure word or repeat the measure word.

items.en: A little over an hour
items.wrongPy: yí gè duō gè xiǎo shí
items.why: The measure word must occur only once before 多; “一个多小时” is correct.

items.en: He exercised for a little over a month.
items.wrongPy: tā yùn dòng le yí gè duō gè yuè
items.why: The measure word must occur only once before 多; “他运动了一个多月” is correct.

items.note: Place 自己 after the subject and before the verb phrase when the subject acts personally or independently. Learners often move 自己 before the subject, which disrupts this sentence pattern; the subject identifies who is acting.

items.en: She exercises by herself.
items.wrongPy: zì jǐ tā yùn dòng
items.why: 自己 follows the subject here; “她自己运动” is the correct order.

items.en: He plays soccer by himself.
items.wrongPy: zì jǐ tā tī zú qiú
items.why: 自己 follows the subject here; “他自己踢足球” is the correct order.

items.note: Here 都 marks an emphatic state that has already been reached, often later or to a greater extent than expected. Put 都 before the situation and 了 at the end. Learners may wrongly assume 都 always means “all.”

items.en: He’s already back.
items.wrongPy: tā huí dōu lái le
items.why: 都 must precede the situation 回来了; the correct order is 他都回来了.

items.en: I’m already all set.
items.wrongPy: wǒ zhǔn bèi hǎo dōu le
items.why: 都 is misplaced after the completed situation; the correct phrase is 我都准备好了.

items.en: She has already started swimming.
items.wrongPy: tā kāi shǐ yóu yǒng dōu le
items.why: 都 cannot go after the situation here; the correct phrase is 她都开始游泳了.

items.note: 正 goes before the verb phrase to show that an action is in progress at that moment; 呢 can mark the ongoing tone at the end. Learners may put 正 after the verb phrase, where it does not mark the action correctly.

Place 呢 at the end of a context-dependent question, such as asking about someone or something in turn. It is not a universal replacement for 吗. Learners may put 呢 inside the clause, breaking the question structure.

items.en: What about him, then?
items.wrongPy: ne nà tā
items.why: 呢 belongs at the end of the question, not before 那他; the correct phrase is 那他呢？

items.en: How is she feeling?
items.wrongPy: tā zěn me yàng ne shēn tǐ
items.why: 呢 belongs at the end of the question clause; the correct phrase is 她身体怎么样呢？

items.note: Put 着 immediately after a verb to describe an ongoing state or activity, especially with verbs like 拿 and 看. It is not a general substitute for 正在: learners often place 着 before the verb, but it follows the verb.

items.en: He is holding a ball.
items.wrongPy: tā zhe ná qiú
items.why: 着 follows the verb 拿, so the correct order is 他拿着球。

items.en: She is looking at the picture.
items.wrongPy: tā zhe kàn huà ne
items.why: 着 follows the verb 看, so the correct order is 她看着画呢。

items.note: Use 因为 before a circumstance noun phrase, then give the result in a separate clause. This differs from a full because-clause. Learners sometimes put 因为 after the reason; it must introduce the reason, as in 因为考试.

items.en: She’s tired because of the exam.
items.wrongPy: kǎo shì yīn wèi tā hěn lèi
items.why: 因为 must come before the reason noun phrase, so write 因为考试，她很累。

items.phrase: 因为运动她身体很舒服
items.zh: 因为运动，她身体很舒服。
items.en: Because of exercise, she feels good.
items.wrong: 运动因为，她身体很舒服。
items.wrongPy: yùn dòng yīn wèi tā shēn tǐ hěn shū fu
items.why: 因为 must precede the reason 运动, giving 因为运动，她身体很舒服。

items.phrase: 因为运动他身体很舒服
items.zh: 因为运动，他身体很舒服。
items.en: Because of exercise, he feels good.
items.wrong: 运动因为，他身体很舒服。
items.wrongPy: yùn dòng yīn wèi tā shēn tǐ hěn shū fu
items.why: 因为 must precede the reason 运动, giving 因为运动，他身体很舒服。

items.note: Attach 什么的 after example items to mean “and similar things,” not to ask what. 都 belongs with the complete list; learners may put 都 between 什么的 and the judgment or treat 什么 as a question word.

items.phrase: 红茶咖啡什么的都不错
items.zh: 红茶、咖啡什么的都不错。
items.en: Black tea, coffee, and things like that are all pretty good.
items.wrong: 红茶、咖啡都什么的不错。
items.wrongPy: hóng chá kā fēi dōu shén me de bú cuò
items.why: 什么的 follows the example list and 都 precedes the judgment, so write 红茶、咖啡什么的都不错。

items.phrase: 足球篮球什么的都好玩儿
items.zh: 足球、篮球什么的都好玩儿。
items.en: Soccer, basketball, and things like that are fun.
items.wrong: 足球、篮球都什么的好玩儿。
items.wrongPy: zú qiú lán qiú dōu shén me de hǎo wánr
items.why: 什么的 follows the example list and 都 precedes the judgment, so write 足球、篮球什么的都好玩儿。

items.note: Sentence-final 吧 softens a tentative judgment or invites confirmation. It does not turn a statement into a suggestion; learners may move it before the subject or modal, but it belongs at the end.

items.en: He’s probably tired.
items.wrongPy: tā kě néng ba hěn lèi
items.why: 吧 softens the whole tentative judgment and belongs at the end, as in 他可能很累吧。

items.en: He may be up ahead, I suppose.
items.wrongPy: tā kě néng ba zài qián miàn
items.why: 吧 softens the whole tentative judgment and belongs at the end, as in 他可能在前面吧。

items.note: Put 的 after an assured statement to add a confident “I’m sure” tone. It is not possessive 的 and does not mark a 是……的 event focus. Learners may mistake it for an object marker; here it simply closes the assured statement.

items.en: He knows, I’m sure.
items.wrongPy: zhī dào tā de
items.why: As a standalone statement, this order leaves 的 dangling; put the subject first, as in 他知道的。

items.note: When learning or teaching results in a skill, place 会 immediately after 学 or 教 and before the skill: 学会游泳. Here 会 marks acquired mastery, not the modal “can” before a verb; 了 can mark the resulting change.

items.en: She learned to swim.
items.wrongPy: tā xué yóu yǒng huì le
items.why: 会 must follow 学 and come before the skill; placing it after 游泳 is wrong.

items.en: He taught me to play soccer.
items.wrongPy: tā jiāo wǒ tī zú qiú huì le
items.why: 会 must follow 教 and precede the skill; it cannot come after 踢足球 here.

items.note: To state a measurable difference, put the difference quantity after the adjective: 高一米. Learners often move the quantity before the adjective, but that position does not express the standard “one meter taller” comparison.

items.en: He is one meter taller than me.
items.wrongPy: tā bǐ wǒ yì mǐ gāo
items.why: The difference quantity follows the adjective; say 高一米, not 一米高.

items.phrase: 这条路比那条路长一米
items.zh: 这条路比那条路长一米。
items.en: This road is one meter longer than that road.
items.wrong: 这条路比那条路一米长。
items.wrongPy: zhè tiáo lù bǐ nà tiáo lù yì mǐ cháng
items.why: The difference quantity follows the adjective; say 长一米, not 一米长.

items.note: 有……这么/那么…… expresses whether one item reaches the reference item's degree, with the adjective following 这么 or 那么. The reference item comes before 这么; learners often put the degree word after the adjective.

items.en: Is he as tall as you?
items.wrongPy: tā yǒu nǐ gāo zhè me ma
items.why: 这么 must come before 高, not after it.

items.en: Is he as tall as I am?
items.wrongPy: tā yǒu wǒ gāo zhè me ma
items.why: 这么 must come before 高, not after it.

items.note: Put the measured amount after the adjective to state how much greater a quality is; the comparison can be understood from context, or stated with 比. Learners often put the amount before the adjective, which breaks the intended difference pattern.

items.en: That road is one meter longer.
items.wrongPy: nà tiáo lù cháng mǐ yī
items.why: The amount must follow 长; the correct order is 那条路长一米.

items.phrase: 这条路比那条路长一米
items.zh: 这条路比那条路长一米。
items.en: This road is one meter longer than that road.
items.wrong: 这条路长比那条路一米。
items.wrongPy: zhè tiáo lù cháng bǐ nà tiáo lù yì mǐ
items.why: The 比 phrase comes before 长 and the amount follows 长, as in 这条路比那条路长一米.

items.note: A directional or result complement follows a motion verb to show movement out, across, and so on; an object can follow the complement. 向北 gives the direction before 过. Learners often move the complement after its object.

items.en: He ran out the door.
items.wrongPy: tā pǎo mén chū le
items.why: 出 must follow 跑 and precede 门; the correct order is 他跑出门了.

items.en: I recognized his name by listening.
items.wrongPy: wǒ tīng tā de chū xìng míng le
items.why: 出 follows 听 and precedes its object; the correct order is 我听出他的姓名了.

items.note: Put 比 and the reference item before the action, then use 得 plus an adjective to compare performance. Learners often put 得 before the action instead of after the verb or verb phrase.

items.en: He swims faster than I do.
items.wrongPy: tā bǐ wǒ de yóu kuài
items.why: 得 follows the action verb 游; the correct order is 他比我游得快.

items.en: He plays soccer better than I do.
items.wrongPy: tā bǐ wǒ tī de zú qiú tī hǎo
items.why: 得 follows the completed action phrase, not 踢; the correct order is 他比我踢足球踢得好.

items.note: Put 得 after the action, then place 比 and the reference item inside the performance complement before the adjective. Learners often move 比 before the action or put 得 after 比.

items.en: He swims faster than I do.
items.wrongPy: tā yóu bǐ wǒ de kuài
items.why: 得 follows 游 before the 比 phrase; the correct order is 他游得比我快.

items.en: He plays ball better than I do.
items.wrongPy: tā tī qiú tī bǐ wǒ de hǎo
items.why: 得 follows 踢 before 比; the correct order is 他踢球踢得比我好.

items.note: 叫 + person + verb phrase means telling or having that person do something; it is not simply a way to name someone. Put the person immediately after 叫 and before the requested action; learners often place the person after the action.

items.en: He told me to take the bag.
items.wrongPy: tā jiào ná bāo wǒ
items.why: The person must follow 叫 and precede the action; say 他叫我拿包。

items.en: He told me to return his schoolbag to him.
items.wrongPy: tā jiào wǒ hái gěi shū bāo tā
items.why: The recipient must come after 给 and before the item; say 他叫我还给他书包。

items.note: 请 + person + verb phrase asks or invites that person to do the action. The person is understood as the subject of the action, so place them after 请 and before the verb phrase; learners often put them after the action.

items.en: I invited him to play ball.
items.wrongPy: wǒ qǐng tī qiú tā
items.why: The invited person must follow 请 and precede the action; say 我请他踢球。

items.en: I invite him to play basketball.
items.wrongPy: wǒ qǐng dǎ lán qiú tā
items.why: The invited person must follow 请 and precede the action; say 我请他打篮球。

items.note: 可能 goes before a predicate to say that an event or state is possible. Use it for likelihood, not learned ability. Learners often put it after the predicate; keep it before the action or state it modifies.

items.en: He might test you.
items.wrongPy: tā kǎo kě néng nǐ
items.why: 可能 must come before 考你; the correct order is 他可能考你。

items.en: He may be up ahead, I suppose.
items.wrongPy: tā kě néng qián miàn zài ba
items.why: 在前面 must stay together after 可能; the correct order is 他可能在前面吧。

items.en: He may have to leave the city.
items.wrongPy: tā kě néng lí kāi chéng shì yào
items.why: 要 must precede 离开; the correct order is 他可能要离开城市。

items.note: Put 地 between a manner phrase and the action it describes: 快乐地笑 means “laugh happily.” Use this pattern to make the manner explicit. Learners often put 地 after the subject; it belongs after the manner phrase, not before it.

items.en: He diligently practices the lesson.
items.wrongPy: tā nǔ lì de kè wén liàn xí
items.why: 课文 belongs after the verb 练习 here; say 他努力地练习课文。

items.note: Place 着 after a verb to describe a state or posture that continues. It differs from 在 plus a verb, which can mark an unfolding activity; learners often put 着 before the verb.

items.en: He is holding a bag.
items.wrongPy: tā zhe ná bāo
items.why: 着 follows the verb 拿, so the correct order is 他拿着包。

items.en: He is holding a soccer ball.
items.wrongPy: tā ná zú qiú zhe
items.why: 着 must follow 拿, not the object 足球, so say 他拿着足球。

items.en: He is standing at the hotel.
items.wrongPy: tā zài bīn guǎn zhe zhàn
items.why: 着 follows the posture verb 站, so the correct order is 他在宾馆站着。

items.en: He is standing in front of me.
items.wrongPy: tā zài miàn qián wǒ zhàn zhe
items.why: 我 must precede 面前 in this location phrase, so the correct order is 他在我面前站着。

items.note: Put 还 before the predicate to say that an earlier action or state continues. It can come before 在 or 很 as part of the predicate. Learners sometimes place 还 after the first verb or after the predicate, confusing its position with additive 还.

items.en: She is still exercising.
items.wrongPy: tā zài hái yùn dòng
items.why: 还 should precede the predicate 在运动; the correct phrase is 她还在运动.

items.en: My younger sister is still at home.
items.wrongPy: mèi mei zài hái jiā
items.why: 还 belongs before 在家, not between 在 and 家; the correct phrase is 妹妹还在家.

items.en: I still need one more opportunity.
items.wrongPy: wǒ chà hái yí gè jī huì
items.why: 还 must precede the predicate 差一个机会; the correct phrase is 我还差一个机会.

items.note: For literal upward movement, 起来 follows the motion verb, as in 站起来. This point is about rising or getting up, not the later extension meaning “begin to.” Learners may mistakenly put 起来 before the verb.

items.en: The tree started growing.
items.wrongPy: shù qǐ lai cháng le
items.why: 起来 must follow 长 in this phrase; the correct order is 树长起来了。

items.en: He stood up.
items.wrongPy: tā qǐ lai zhàn le
items.why: 起来 must follow 站, not precede it; the correct phrase is 他站起来了。
